column2: 中古英语 wykeday ← 古英语 wicdæġ ← 原始日耳曼语 *wikadagaz，即 week ＋ day
column3: any day of the week other than Saturday and Sunday
column5: The museum is quieter on a weekday.|Buses run more often on weekdays.
column6: one of the days when ordinary business goes on – 照常办事的那几天里的一天
column7: 平日：与周末相对的那几天|上班日：其中要去上班的那几天

column2: 由 week ＋ end 复合而成；原为英格兰北部方言，19 世纪末进入通用语
column3: Saturday and Sunday, when most people do not work
column5: We drove to the coast for the weekend.|She works most weekends at the shop.
column6: the pair of days at the end of the week when work stops – 一周末尾停工的那两天

column2: 中古英语 wykely，即 week ＋ 副词或形容词后缀 -ly
column3: happening once every week
column5: The magazine appears weekly on Thursdays.|They hold a weekly meeting every Monday.
column6: coming round once in each seven-day turn – 每七天一轮里出现一次
column7: 每周：以周为间隔|每周一次：明说频率是一周一回

column2: 中古英语 wepen ← 古英语 wēpan（哭、哀叹）← 原始日耳曼语 *wōpijaną（哭）← 原始印欧语 *weh₂b-（呼、诉）
column3: to cry, letting tears fall
column5: She wept when she heard the news.|He wept openly at the graveside.
column6: crying with tears coming down – 出声或不出声地哭，泪水往下落
column7: 哭泣：出于悲痛而哭|落泪：眼泪流下来这件事

column2: 中古英语 weyen ← 古英语 wegan（搬动、称）← 原始日耳曼语 *weganą（移动、承载、称）← 原始印欧语 *weǵʰ-（运送）；与 wagon、way 同源
column3: to find out how heavy something is, or to consider carefully
column5: He weighed the parcel at the post office.|She weighed the risks before agreeing.
column6: putting something on the scale to see how much it comes to – 放到秤上，看它有多少
column7: 称重：量出物体有多重|权衡：把利弊放到心里的秤上比一比

column2: 中古英语 weight ← 古英语 ġewiht ← 原始日耳曼语 *wihtiz ← 原始印欧语 *weǵʰ-（运送、拉）；即 weigh ＋ 抽象名词后缀 -t
column3: how heavy something is, or a piece of metal used on scales
column5: What is the weight of this case?|He lifted weights every morning.
column6: how much a thing presses down – 一件东西向下压的程度
column7: 分量：物体轻重的程度|砝码：秤上用来比对的那块金属|负担：把这份下压用到心事或责任上

column2: 中古英语 werde ← 古英语 wyrd（命运）← 原始日耳曼语 *wurdiz ← 原始印欧语 *wert-（转）；16 世纪已废，由莎士比亚以 Weird Sisters（命运三女神）之名重新带回
column3: strange in a way that feels uncanny or unsettling
column5: A weird noise came from the loft.|That was a weird thing to say.
column6: strange enough to leave one uneasy – 怪得让人心里发毛
column7: 古怪的：与常态不合，让人费解|离奇的：奇到近乎不可思议

column2: 中古英语 welcome ← 古英语 wilcuma（受欢迎的客人）← 原始日耳曼语 *wiljakwemô（如愿而来的人），即 will（愿）＋ come（来者）；后因第二成分的「客」义失落，wil- 受副词 well 影响改作 wel-
column3: gladly received, or to greet someone gladly
column5: You are always welcome here.|They welcomed us at the door.
column6: received as someone whose coming was wished for – 被当作正盼着他来的人接待
column7: 受欢迎的：来了让人高兴的|欢迎：把这份高兴表示出来这个动作

column2: 英语 weld 是 well（沸、涌）的变体，或受其过去分词 welled 影响；与丹麦语 vælde、瑞典语 välla（沸腾、锻接）同族
column3: to join pieces of metal by heating them until they fuse
column5: They welded the frame in place.|A crack appeared along the weld.
column6: joining metal by melting the edges into one – 把金属边缘熔到一起，合成一体
column7: 焊接：把金属熔合到一起这个工艺|焊缝：熔合处留下的那道痕

column2: 中古英语 welefare，或出自古英语短语 wel faran（过得好）；即 well ＋ fare。「社会救助」义 1904 年始见
column3: the health and comfort of people, or help given by the state
column5: The scheme looks after the welfare of staff.|She lived on welfare for two years.
column6: how well people are doing, and the help that keeps them so – 人过得好不好，以及维持这份好的援助
column7: 福利：为保障生活而提供的待遇或救助|安康：身心状况良好这件事

column2: 副词 ← 中古英语 wel ← 古英语 wel（好、充分）← 原始日耳曼语 *wela（如愿地）← 原始印欧语 *welh₁-（愿、要）；名词「井」是另一支，← 古英语 wielle（泉）
column3: in a good or satisfactory way, or a hole dug for water
column5: She sings well for her age.|They drew water from the well.
column6: as one would wish it to be – 事情如人所愿的那个样子
column7: 好：合乎期望地，做得到位|充分地：程度够足，如「充分知情」|井：打到地下取水的那个洞，是同形异源的另一支

column2: 中古英语 west ← 古英语 west ← 原始日耳曼语 *westrą ← 原始印欧语 *wek⁽ʷ⁾speros（傍晚），因日落方向而得名
column3: the direction in which the sun goes down
column5: The road runs west from here.|Storms come in from the west.
column6: the side of the sky where the sun goes down – 太阳落下去的那一边
column7: 西：四方之一|西方：那一侧的地带或阵营

column2: 中古英语 westerne ← 古英语 westerne ← 原始日耳曼语 *westrōnijaz，即 west ＋ -ern
column3: situated in or coming from the west
column5: The western slope gets less sun.|A western wind brought rain.
column6: belonging to the side where the sun sets – 属于日落那一侧的
column7: 西面的：位置在西|西部的：属于某地西边那一片

column2: 中古英语 wet，是 weten（弄湿）的过去分词 ← 古英语 wǣtan（弄湿）← 原始日耳曼语 *wētijaną ← 原始印欧语 *wed-（水、湿）；与 water 同源
column3: covered or soaked with liquid
column5: His shoes were wet through.|Rain wet the whole field.
column6: having taken up liquid so it is no longer dry – 吸了液体，不再是干的
column7: 湿的：表面或内里带着水|潮的：湿的程度轻，带着水气|淋湿：使某物变湿这个动作

column2: 中古英语 whal ← 古英语 hwæl ← 原始日耳曼语 *hwalaz（鲸）← 原始印欧语 *(s)kʷálos（一种大鱼）
column3: a very large sea animal that breathes air
column5: A whale surfaced beside the boat.|Whales migrate along this coast.
column6: a huge sea animal that must surface to breathe – 极大的海中动物，得浮上来呼吸

column2: 中古英语 whatever，即 what ＋ -ever
column3: anything at all, no matter what
column5: Take whatever you need from the shelf.|Whatever happens, try to stay calm.
column6: any one of them, the choice making no difference – 其中任意一个，选哪个都不影响
column7: 无论什么：不限于哪一样|任何：泛指全体中的任一

column2: 中古英语 whete ← 古英语 hwǣte ← 原始西日耳曼语 *hwaitī ← 原始日耳曼语 *hwaitijaz ← *hwītaz（白），因磨出的粉色白而得名
column3: the grain used to make flour and bread
column5: The wheat ripens in late July.|Bread is made from wheat flour.
column6: the grain ground into the flour most bread is made from – 磨成面粉、多数面包所用的那种谷物
column7: 小麦：这种作物的正式名称|麦子：日常说法，泛指其籽粒

column2: 中古英语 whel ← 古英语 hwēol ← 原始日耳曼语 *hwehwlą ← 原始印欧语 *kʷekʷlóm，是 *kʷel-（转）的重叠形，字面「不停转的那个东西」
column3: a round object that turns on an axle
column5: One wheel came off the trolley.|He gripped the wheel with both hands.
column6: a round thing that turns on a centre so a load can roll – 绕中心转动的圆件，使载重可以滚着走
column7: 轮子：车上转动的那个圆件|方向盘：司机手握、用来转向的那个轮

column2: 中古英语 whan evere，即 when ＋ -ever
column3: at any time that, or every time that
column5: Come round whenever you like.|Whenever it rains, the road floods.
column6: at any time it happens, without exception – 只要发生，任何一次都算
column7: 每当：每一次那种情形出现时|无论何时：不限定在哪个时刻

column2: 由 where ＋ -ever 构成；where 一支 ← 古英语 hwǣr（何处）← 原始日耳曼语 *hwar
column3: in or to any place that
column5: Sit wherever you like in the hall.|Wherever she goes, the dog follows.
column6: in any place at all, the place making no difference – 任何地方都算，在哪儿不影响
column7: 无论哪里：不限定在哪个地方|凡所在之处：所到的每一处都如此

column2: 由 which ＋ -ever 构成；which 一支 ← 古英语 hwilc（哪一个）← 原始日耳曼语 *hwilīkaz
column3: any one of a set, no matter which
column5: Take whichever seat you prefer.|Whichever route you choose is fine.
column6: any one out of the set, the choice making no difference – 那一组里任取一个，选哪个都行

column2: 中古英语 whippen ← 中古荷兰语 wippen（摆动、跳）与中古低地德语 wippen（快速动）← 原始日耳曼语 *wippōną（来回动）← 原始印欧语 *weyp-（摇、甩）；wh- 是模拟鞭响的写法
column3: a long thin strip used for striking, or to beat cream stiff
column5: He cracked the whip above the horses.|Whip the cream until it thickens.
column6: a long flexible strip swung to strike – 甩出去打人的那条长软带
column7: 鞭子：那件甩打之物|抽打：用它击打这个动作|搅打：把奶油之类快速搅到发起，动作也是这么甩

column2: 中古英语 whirlen，缩自 *whirvelen，或 ← 古英语 *hwyrflian（hweorfan「转」的反复体）← 原始日耳曼语 *hwerbaną（转）；或 ← 古诺尔斯语 hvirfla（打转）
column3: to turn round and round very fast
column5: Leaves whirled up in the wind.|Her mind whirled with questions.
column6: turning about a centre fast enough to blur – 绕着中心转得快到看不清
column7: 旋转：绕中心不停转动|急转：转得又快又猛|头晕：脑子里像在打转

column2: 英语 whisky 是 usque 的变体，截自 usquebaugh ← 苏格兰盖尔语 uisge-beatha（生命之水），是中世纪拉丁语 aqua vitae 的仿译
column3: a strong alcoholic drink made from grain
column5: He poured two glasses of whisky.|The whisky had aged twelve years.
column6: a strong spirit distilled from grain and aged in wood – 用谷物蒸出、在木桶里存过的烈酒

column2: 中古英语 whisperen ← 古英语 hwisprian（低语）← 原始日耳曼语 *hwisprōną（嘶、低语）← 原始印欧语 *ḱwey-（嘶、吹）；与 whistle 同支
column3: to speak very quietly, using breath rather than voice
column5: She whispered something in his ear.|Do not whisper during the exam.
column6: speaking on breath alone so only the nearest can hear – 只用气不用声，近处的人才听得见
column7: 低声说：把声音压到很小|耳语：贴着耳朵说，旁人听不到

column2: 中古英语 whistel ← 古英语 hwistle ← 动词 hwistlan（吹哨）← 原始日耳曼语 *hwistlōną（发出嘶声）
column3: a high sound made by blowing, or the object used to make it
column5: The referee blew his whistle.|He whistled a tune as he walked.
column6: a high thin sound forced out through a narrow opening – 气流从窄口挤出所发的又高又细的音
column7: 哨声：吹出来的那个高音|口哨：用嘴唇吹出的那种|吹哨：发出这种声音这个动作

column2: 中古英语 whit ← 古英语 hwīt ← 原始日耳曼语 *hwītaz ← 原始印欧语 *ḱweydós，是 *ḱweytós（明亮、发光）的变体
column3: of the colour of snow or milk
column5: She wore a plain white shirt.|Paint the ceiling white before you move in.
column6: the colour that gives back all light and holds none – 把所有光都反回去、自己不留的那种颜色
column7: 白的：形容颜色如雪如乳|白色：那种颜色本身

column2: 中古英语 whoever，即 who ＋ -ever
column3: any person that, no matter who
column5: Whoever finds it should hand it in.|Ask whoever is on duty.
column6: any person at all, the identity making no difference – 任何人都算，是谁并不影响
column7: 无论谁：不限定是哪个人|凡是…的人：符合那个条件的每一个人

column2: 中古英语 whol ← 古英语 hāl（完好的、健全的）← 原始日耳曼语 *hailaz ← 原始印欧语 *kéh₂ilos（健全、完整）；wh- 拼写是 1400 年前后西南方言里衍生的
column3: complete, with no part missing
column5: He ate the whole loaf.|The whole team turned up.
column6: having every part still there, nothing broken off – 各部分都在，没掉没缺
column7: 整个的：作为一体、未被分割|全部的：范围上一个不落

column2: 英语早期作 holesome ← 中古英语 holsom ← 古英语 *hālsum ← 原始日耳曼语 *hailasamaz，即 whole ＋ 形容词后缀 -some
column3: good for the health, or morally sound
column5: They ate simple, wholesome food.|The film is wholesome family fare.
column6: doing good rather than harm to body or character – 对身体或品性有益而无损
column7: 有益健康的：吃了用了对身体好|正派的：内容或为人端正，无不良处
